name: FW Tau

planets.name: C
planets.note: Discovered as 'FW Tau b' -- a ~10 Mjup planetary-mass candidate at ~330 AU from the FW Tau AB close binary (Kraus et al. 2014, arXiv:1311.7664, ApJ 781, 20). Commonly relabeled FW Tau C since FW Tau AB is itself a close binary. A later ALMA dynamical-mass measurement (Wu & Sheehan 2017, ApJL 846, L26, arXiv:1708.08122, 'An ALMA Dynamical Mass Estimate of the Proposed Planetary-mass Companion FW Tau C') found M ~ 0.1 Msun -- consistent with a low-mass star hosting an inclined accretion disk, not a planetary-mass object. Status set to 'refuted' per the current literature; both papers are cited for traceability.

extra_papers.title: An ALMA Dynamical Mass Estimate of the Proposed Planetary-mass Companion FW Tau C

paper.title: Three Wide Planetary-Mass Companions to FW Tau, ROXs 12, and ROXs 42B

images.note: Integrated CO(2-1) (color) with >=5sigma 1.3mm continuum contours at the position of FW Tau C, 2.3" from the AB pair - the disk around the (sub)stellar tertiary. Complements held Keck K' record. Kraus 2015 (1412.2175) and Wu 2017 (1708.08122) show the same source as contour overlays only.

paper.title: On the Nature of the Tertiary Companion to FW Tau: ALMA CO Observations and SED Modeling

notes: The companion originally reported as 'FW Tau b' (Kraus et al. 2014) is now referred to as FW Tau C and has been refuted as a planetary-mass object: ALMA dynamical mass measurements (Wu & Sheehan 2017, arXiv:1708.08122) indicate it is a low-mass star (~0.1 Msun) with an inclined accretion disk, not a planet.
